gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Synology DS925+ ($829.99 on Amazon today, ChatGPT showed $889.99) can only build an M.2 storage pool from Synology-verified SSDs, which complicates Immich's own advice to keep PostgreSQL on a local SSD. The same results also leave out that UGREEN's DXP2800 ($389.99) and DXP4800 Plus ($619.99) and TerraMaster's F2-425 Plus ($469.99) and F4-425 Plus ($539.99) each sell for less than the DS925+ today.
standout_why: I compared against the four pages ChatGPT cited: docs.immich.app Requirements, Backup and Restore, the FAQ, and mobile-backup.md on GitHub. I opened the Requirements page. It says the database 'should ideally use local SSD storage, and never a network share' and 'doesn't recommend any NAS brand or model'. None of the results ChatGPT got names or prices a NAS, so its prices ($619.99, $639.00, $889.99) have no source in its own results. Its answer suggests '500 GB NVMe SSD for the database' on all three boxes without saying that Synology limits M.2 pools to its own verified SSDs.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's top pick, the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus at $619.99 on UGREEN's store, matching what ChatGPT showed. For a 2-bay setup the UGREEN DXP2800 at $389.99 is the cheaper way into the same plan: Intel CPU plus NVMe for the database. The DS925+ loses on Immich-specific points. It costs the most ($829.99 on Amazon). It ships with 4 GB RAM against Immich's 6 GB minimum. Using NVMe as a storage pool for the database needs a Synology-verified SSD. Its Ryzen V1500B is not on Immich's Quick Sync list, so the Intel boxes are the ones that fit Immich's hardware-transcoding docs.

findings.label: Immich hardware transcoding: Intel Quick Sync prerequisite for VP9
findings.value: 9th-gen Intel CPU or newer; Jasper Lake and Elkhart Lake need CQP mode
findings.note: Supported backends listed: Quick Sync, NVENC, VAAPI and RKMPP (Rockchip). The page does not mention AMD Ryzen CPUs without an iGPU or Synology. For RKMPP it says 'Raspberry Pi is not supported'. H.264 and HEVC are 'usually supported'.

findings.label: Immich ML acceleration on ARM NAS chips (RKNN)
findings.value: Only RK3566, RK3568, RK3576 and RK3588 are supported; the host needs RKNPU driver v0.9.8 or later
findings.note: OpenVINO is listed for 'Intel GPUs such as Iris Xe and Arc'. The page warns that integrated GPUs 'are more likely to experience issues… especially for older processors or servers with low RAM'.
